# iliad-121 (18.509–617) — new renderings

Format: Greek (line) | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἐν δ’ ἐτίθει (541, 550, 561, 607) · ἐν δὲ … ποίησε (573, 587) · ἐν δὲ … ποίκιλλε (590) | "And on it he set" · "And on it he made" · "wrought intricately" | same (with "worked an intricate" in `i` at 590) | "In it", "Therein"; "set" for τίθημι and "made" for ποιέω keep the two verbs apart, as the previous part has "And on it he made" (18.490) |
| ἔριθοι (550) | "hired labourers" | "hired labourers" | "reapers" (they are named by ἤμων), "workmen" |
| τέμενος βασιλήϊον (550) | "a royal precinct" | "a king’s estate" | "sanctuary", "grove"; follows the Odyssey’s τέμενος "precinct" (`l`) / "estate" (`i`) of ploughland |
| ἀμαλλοδετῆρες (553, 554) | "sheaf-binders" | "sheaf-binders" | "binders" alone, "gleaners" |
| ἐλλεδανοῖσι (553; rare word) | "with bands" | "with bands" (+ note: rare, sense not quite certain) | "with straw ropes" (adds the material) |
| δραγμεύοντες (555; rare verb) | "gathering handfuls" | "gathered up the handfuls" | "binding" |
| ἀλωή (561, 566) | "vineyard" | "vineyard" | "orchard", "garden"; the grapes and the vintage decide, as at Odyssey 7.122 |
| κάμαξ (563) | "poles" | "poles" ("silver poles") | "stakes", "props", "trellises" |
| κάπετος κυανέη (564) | "dark ditch" | "dark ditch" | "dark-blue" (turned down in the table), "black", "steel-blue", "enamel"; κυανέη keeps "dark" as for the brows (1.528) and the cloud (5.345) |
| φορῆες (566) | "carriers" | "carriers" | "bearers", "pickers" |
| ἀταλὰ φρονέοντες (567) | "thinking tender thoughts" | "with tender thoughts in their hearts" | "light-hearted", "innocent", "carefree" (turned down at ἀταλάφρων, 6.400) |
| ἱμερόεν κιθάριζε (570) · ἱμερόεντα χορόν (603) | "full of longing" | "with a sound full of longing" · "full of longing" | "lovely", "sweetly"; ἱμερόεις keeps "full of longing" (Odyssey 18.194, Iliad 3.397) |
| λίνον … ἄειδε (570; uncertain) | "the Linos-song" | "the song of Linos" (+ note: or the lyre’s linen string, "sang to the string") | "the string", "a dirge" (each commits) |
| ῥήσσοντες ἁμαρτῇ (571) | "stamping together" | "stamping together" (+ note: literally "striking") | "beating the ground" (supplies the object), "breaking into song" |
| ἰυγμός (572) | "shouting" | "whoops" | "cries", "shrieks" |
| σμερδαλέω λέοντε (579) | "frightful lions" | "frightful lions" | "terrible", "dread" (σμερδαλέος keeps "frightful", 12.91) |
| ἐρύγμηλος (580) | "bellowing" | "bellowing" | "roaring", "belching" |
| κόπρος (575) | "dung-yard" | "farmyard" | "stable", "dung-hill" ; the Odyssey’s κόπρος is "dung" |
| ῥοδανὸν δονακῆα (576; rare, sense not certain) | "swaying reed-bed" | "swaying reed-bed" (+ note: rare, sense not certain) | "rustling reeds", "waving rushes" |
| κελάδοντα (ποταμόν, 576) | "resounding" | "loud" | "roaring", "babbling"; κέλαδος "din" (9.547) |
| ἀργοί (πόδας ἀργοί, 578) | "swift in foot" | "swift" | follows the table’s κύνες ἀργοί "swift dogs" (disputed, "swift" or "white") |
| ἐνδίεσαν ταχέας κύνας ὀτρύνοντες (584) | "were setting on the swift dogs, urging them" | "set the swift dogs on … urging them forward" | "baited", "sicked" |
| ἀπετρωπῶντο (585) · ἀλέοντο (586) | "were shrinking back" · "kept dodging" | "shrank" · "kept dodging out of the way" | "refused", "were afraid" |
| σταθμοί (589) | "steadings" | "steadings" | "stalls", "folds"; follows the table’s σταθμός "steading" |
| ἀλφεσίβοιαι (593; sense not quite certain) | "ox-earning" | "who bring their families oxen" (+ note: usual explanation) | "worth oxen", "bride-price" alone |
| χορός (590, 603) | "dancing-ground" | "dancing-ground" | "dance" (the place decides here; the dance on it is in the note) |
| ὀθόνας (595) | "fine linen cloths" | "fine linen robes" | "veils", "sheets" |
| χιτῶνας … ἐϋννήτους (596) | "well-spun tunics" | "well-spun tunics" | "well-woven" (νέω "spin") |
| στεφάναι (597) | "garlands" | "garlands" | "crowns" (reserved for στέφανος as a ring), "wreaths" |
| μαχαίρας … ἐξ ἀργυρέων τελαμώνων (598) | "knives of gold from silver straps" | "golden knives from silver straps" | "daggers", "swords", "baldrics"; μάχαιρα "knife" (11.844), τελαμών "strap" |
| ἐπισταμένοισι πόδεσσι (599) | "knowing feet" | "skilful feet" | "practised", "nimble" |
| ἐπὶ στίχας (602) | "in rows toward one another" | "in lines to meet one another" | "in ranks" |
| ἐμέλπετο (604) | "was celebrating" | "made music" | "sang" alone (the Greek has φορμίζων for the lyre) |
| κυβιστητῆρε (605) | "tumblers" | "tumblers" | follows the table (16.750) |
| ἄντυγα … πυμάτην (608) | "outermost rim" | "outermost rim" | follows the table’s ἄντυξ "rim" of a shield (6.118) |
| σάκεος πύκα ποιητοῖο (608) | "well-wrought shield" | "well-made shield" | "stoutly built" ("stout" kept for στιβαρός) |
| θώρηκα φαεινότερον πυρὸς αὐγῆς (610) | "a breastplate brighter than the gleam of fire" | same | "shining" is reserved for φαεινός; the comparative is "brighter" |
| ἑανοῦ κασσιτέροιο (613; sense not certain) | "of pliant tin" | "of pliant tin" (+ note: sense not certain) | "fine", "soft", "ductile" |
| ὅπλα (614) · τεύχεα (617) | "arms" · "armour" | "armour" · "armour" | "gear" (the table’s ὅπλα in a smith’s workshop, 18.409, and tackle in the Odyssey); τεύχεα keeps "armour" |
| κλυτὸς ἀμφιγυήεις (614) | "the famous both-limbed one" | "the famous both-limbed god" | "very famous" (περικλυτός, 587, 590, keeps the table’s "very famous both-limbed") |
| Κήρ (ὀλοὴ Κήρ, 535) | "baleful Death-spirit" | "baleful Death-spirit" | "Doom", "Fate" (reserved for μοῖρα, πότμος); capitalised like Ἔρις "Strife", Κυδοιμός "Uproar" as a power; follows the table’s κὴρ θανάτοιο "death-spirit" |
| ἐν δ’ Ἔρις ἐν δὲ Κυδοιμός (535) | "Strife", "Uproar" | "Strife", "Uproar" | follows the table (4.440, 5.593) |
| ὀλοή (535) | "baleful" | "baleful" | "deadly", "ruinous" (reserved for οὐλόμενος) |
| νεούτατος · ἄουτος (536) | "newly wounded" · "unwounded" | "freshly wounded" · "unwounded" | "newly slain", "untouched" |
| εἰράων (531; sense not known) | "the assembly-places" | "their meeting-places" (+ note: sense not known, a guess) | "ridges", "watch-posts", "council" |
| σύριγξι (526) | "reed-pipes" | "reed-pipes" | "flutes" (the table’s αὐλοί "pipes"), "panpipes" |
| μηλοβοτῆρες (529) | "shepherds" | "shepherds" | "herdsmen" (kept for νομῆες), "sheep-herders" |
| ὑπολίζονες (519; rare, formation not certain) | "somewhat smaller" | "smaller" | "slighter", "mean" |
| ἀμφίς … ἀριζήλω (519) | "apart" · "conspicuous" | "apart from the rest" · "plain to see" | "on both sides"; ἀρίζηλος keeps "conspicuous" (18.219) in `l` |
| καλός (518, 562, 588, 597, 611, 612) | "fine" | "fine" | "fair", "beautiful" (kept for parts of the body, σφυρὰ κάλ’, and for καλλι- compounds: καλλιπλοκάμῳ "fair-plaited", 592); adverbial καλὸν ἄειδε (570) is "beautifully"; follows iliad-120 ("fine greaves", "fine armour") |
| δαφοινεός (538; sense not certain) | "blood-red" | "blood-red" (+ note: longer form of δαφοινός, exact sense not certain) | "deep-red", "tawny"; αἵματι is a dative of means |
| δίχα … ἥνδανε βουλή (510) | "in two ways the plan was pleasing to them" | "their counsel was divided" | "of two minds" alone |

Departures from published English: none. The Odyssey line 18.533–534 (στησάμενοι δ’ ἐμάχοντο μάχην παρὰ νηυσὶ θοῇσι) is reused with the place changed to "beside the banks of the river". Ὠκεανοῖο is "Oceanus" (the table), while iliad-120 has "Ocean" at 18.489.
